menuItems.name: Garden Buddha Bowl
menuItems.description: Quinoa, roasted chickpeas, avocado, cucumber, edamame, tahini dressing
menuItems.method: Step 1: Cook quinoa according to package instructions; let cool. Step 2: Preheat oven to 400°F (200°C). Toss chickpeas with 1 tbsp olive oil, salt, and pepper; roast for 20–25 minutes until crispy. Step 3: In a small bowl, whisk tahini, lemon juice, minced garlic, remaining olive oil, water (as needed for consistency), salt, and pepper to make the dressing. Step 4: Assemble bowls by dividing cooled quinoa among serving bowls. Top with roasted chickpeas, sliced avocado, cucumber, and edamame. Drizzle generously with tahini dressing. Serve immediately or chill briefly for a cooler bowl. Optional garnishes include sesame seeds or fresh herbs.

menuItems.name: Spicy Tofu Ramen
menuItems.description: Rich miso broth, silken tofu, ramen noodles, scallions, chili oil
menuItems.method: Step 1: In a pot, heat sesame oil over medium heat. Add garlic and ginger; sauté until fragrant, about 1 minute. Step 2: Add vegetable broth and bring to a simmer. Whisk in miso paste and soy sauce until fully dissolved. Step 3: Gently add silken tofu cubes and simmer for 5 minutes without boiling to preserve texture. Step 4: Meanwhile, cook ramen noodles according to package instructions; drain and divide between two bowls. Step 5: Ladle hot miso broth with tofu over noodles. Drizzle with chili oil to taste and garnish generously with sliced scallions. Serve immediately for a comforting, spicy bowl of ramen with creamy tofu and aromatic broth.

menuItems.name: Mango Green Smoothie
menuItems.description: Fresh mango, spinach, banana, coconut water, chia seeds
menuItems.method: Step 1: Add the fresh spinach and coconut water to a high-speed blender. Blend on low until the spinach is fully broken down. Step 2: Add the diced mango, banana, and chia seeds to the blender. Increase the speed to high and blend until smooth and creamy, about 30–45 seconds. If the mixture is too thick, add a splash more coconut water to reach your desired consistency. Step 3: Pour into a chilled glass and serve immediately for the freshest flavor and maximum nutrient retention. For added texture, you can sprinkle a few extra chia seeds on top before serving. This smoothie is naturally sweet, hydrating, and packed with vitamins, fiber, and healthy omega-3s from the chia seeds.

menuItems.name: Teriyaki Tempeh Plate
menuItems.description: Marinated tempeh, steamed brown rice, broccoli, carrots, teriyaki glaze
menuItems.method: Step 1: Cook brown rice according to package instructions. Step 2: Whisk together soy sauce, maple syrup, rice vinegar, garlic, ginger, and water to make the teriyaki marinade. Slice tempeh into strips and marinate for at least 15 minutes. Step 3: Steam broccoli and carrots until tender-crisp, about 5–7 minutes. Step 4: In a skillet over medium heat, cook marinated tempeh in sesame oil until golden, about 3–4 minutes per side. Step 5: Remove tempeh, then add reserved marinade to the pan. Mix cornstarch with 1 tsp water and stir into the sauce; simmer until thickened. Step 6: Plate cooked rice, steamed vegetables, and tempeh, then drizzle with teriyaki glaze.

menuItems.name: Cucumber Mint Lemonade
menuItems.description: Fresh cucumber, mint, lemon juice, sparkling water, light agave
menuItems.method: Step 1: In a blender, combine the chopped cucumber, mint leaves, lemon juice, and agave syrup. Blend until smooth. Step 2: Strain the mixture through a fine-mesh sieve into a pitcher to remove pulp and mint fibers, pressing with a spoon to extract all liquid. Step 3: Chill the mixture in the refrigerator for at least 30 minutes or serve immediately over ice. Step 4: Just before serving, gently stir in the sparkling water to preserve its fizz. Pour into glasses filled with ice, garnish with extra mint leaves or cucumber slices if desired, and enjoy immediately for the freshest flavor.

menuItems.name: Rainbow Spring Rolls
menuItems.description: Rice paper rolls with shredded vegetables, mango, mint, peanut dipping sauce
menuItems.method: Step 1: Prepare all vegetables and mango by julienning or thinly slicing them; set aside with mint leaves. Step 2: Make the peanut dipping sauce by whisking together peanut butter, soy sauce, lime juice, honey, and enough water to reach a smooth, dippable consistency. Step 3: Fill a large shallow bowl with warm water. Dip one rice paper wrapper for 10–15 seconds until pliable but still slightly firm. Lay it flat on a damp surface. Step 4: Arrange a small amount of each vegetable, mango, and a few mint leaves in the center of the wrapper. Step 5: Fold the sides inward, then roll tightly from the bottom to enclose the filling. Repeat with remaining wrappers and fillings. Step 6: Serve immediately with peanut dipping sauce, optionally garnished with crushed peanuts.

menuItems.name: Matcha Chia Pudding
menuItems.description: Coconut milk chia pudding with matcha powder, mango chunks, granola
menuItems.method: Step 1: In a bowl or jar, whisk together coconut milk, chia seeds, matcha powder, and sweetener until well combined. Let sit for 5 minutes, then whisk again to prevent clumping. Step 2: Cover and refrigerate for at least 2 hours or overnight, allowing the chia seeds to absorb liquid and form a pudding-like texture. Step 3: Once set, give the pudding a good stir. If it’s too thick, add a splash of coconut milk to reach desired consistency. Step 4: Spoon the matcha chia pudding into serving bowls or glasses. Top with fresh mango chunks and a generous sprinkle of granola for crunch. Serve chilled. This refreshing, nutrient-rich dessert or breakfast combines earthy matcha, creamy coconut, tropical mango, and crunchy granola for a balanced and satisfying dish.

menuItems.name: Sesame Ginger Noodle Salad
menuItems.description: Soba noodles, shredded cabbage, edamame, sesame ginger vinaigrette
menuItems.method: Step 1: Cook soba noodles according to package instructions; rinse under cold water and drain well. Step 2: In a small bowl, whisk together sesame oil, rice vinegar, grated ginger, soy sauce, and honey to make the vinaigrette. Step 3: In a large bowl, combine cooled noodles, shredded cabbage, edamame, and green onions. Step 4: Pour the dressing over the salad and toss gently until evenly coated. Step 5: Sprinkle toasted sesame seeds on top before serving. Chill for 15 minutes if desired for a refreshing, crisp texture. This vibrant salad balances nutty, tangy, and savory flavors with satisfying crunch and protein-rich edamame.

menuItems.name: Edamame with Sea Salt
menuItems.description: Steamed young soybeans, flaked sea salt, sesame oil, chili flakes
menuItems.method: Step 1: Rinse the edamame pods under cold water and pat dry. Step 2: Bring a pot of salted water to a boil and add the edamame. Steam or boil for 4–5 minutes until bright green and tender. Step 3: Drain thoroughly and transfer to a serving bowl. Step 4: While still warm, drizzle with sesame oil and sprinkle evenly with flaked sea salt and chili flakes. Step 5: Toss gently to coat the pods evenly. Serve immediately while warm, encouraging guests to squeeze the beans directly from the pods into their mouths. This simple preparation highlights the natural sweetness of the soybeans while the sea salt adds crunch, the sesame oil lends nuttiness, and the chili flakes provide a subtle kick. Perfect as an appetizer or healthy snack.

menuItems.name: Miso Soup with Wakame
menuItems.description: White miso broth, silken tofu, wakame seaweed, scallions, toasted sesame
menuItems.method: Step 1: Rehydrate the dried wakame by soaking it in warm water for 5 minutes until tender; drain and set aside. Step 2: In a medium pot, gently heat the water or dashi over medium-low heat—do not boil. Step 3: In a small bowl, whisk the white miso paste with a ladleful of the warm liquid until smooth, then stir it back into the pot. Step 4: Add the rehydrated wakame and silken tofu cubes, and simmer gently for 2–3 minutes to meld flavors without boiling (boiling can ruin miso’s probiotics). Step 5: Remove from heat, ladle into bowls, and garnish with sliced scallions and a sprinkle of toasted sesame seeds. Serve immediately while warm.

menuItems.name: Avocado Tartare
menuItems.description: Diced avocado, mango, cucumber, sesame oil, pickled ginger, nori chips
menuItems.method: Step 1: In a medium bowl, gently combine the diced avocado, mango, and cucumber. Be careful not to mash the avocado—use a light hand to keep the texture intact. Step 2: Add the sesame oil and finely chopped pickled ginger, then fold everything together until evenly coated. Taste and adjust if needed, though the pickled ginger adds both tang and saltiness. Step 3: Let the mixture rest for 5–10 minutes to allow flavors to meld slightly. Step 4: Just before serving, sprinkle crumbled nori chips over the top for crunch and umami depth. Serve immediately on chilled plates or in small bowls to maintain freshness and prevent browning. This dish is best enjoyed right away while the textures are crisp and vibrant.

menuItems.name: Crispy Vegetable Wontons
menuItems.description: Pan-fried vegetable and tofu wontons, chili oil dipping sauce, sesame seeds
menuItems.method: Step 1: Press tofu to remove excess water, then crumble into a bowl. Add grated carrot, chopped cabbage, green onions, garlic, and ginger. Mix well. Season with soy sauce and sesame oil. Step 2: Place 1 tsp of filling in the center of each wonton wrapper. Moisten edges with water, fold into triangles or rectangles, and seal tightly. Step 3: Heat vegetable oil in a non-stick pan over medium heat. Arrange wontons in a single layer and pan-fry until golden brown and crispy on both sides (about 2–3 minutes per side). Step 4: Serve hot with chili oil drizzled on top or as a dipping sauce, garnished with toasted sesame seeds.

menuItems.name: Coconut Mango Sorbet
menuItems.description: Fresh coconut cream sorbet, diced mango, toasted coconut flakes, lime zest
menuItems.method: Step 1: In a saucepan, gently heat the coconut cream and sugar over medium-low heat, stirring until the sugar fully dissolves. Do not boil. Remove from heat and let cool completely, then chill in the refrigerator for at least 2 hours. Step 2: Pour the chilled mixture into an ice cream maker and churn according to manufacturer’s instructions until it reaches a soft-serve consistency. Step 3: Transfer half of the sorbet into a freezer-safe container. Gently fold in the diced mango, then layer or swirl the remaining plain sorbet on top. Step 4: Sprinkle with toasted coconut flakes and lime zest. Freeze for at least 3–4 hours or until firm. Let sit at room temperature for 5 minutes before serving to soften slightly.

menuItems.name: Black Sesame Tofu Panna Cotta
menuItems.description: Silken tofu panna cotta, black sesame paste swirl, poached Asian pear, honey
menuItems.method: Step 1: Blend silken tofu, 2 tablespoons honey, vanilla extract, and agar-agar powder until smooth. Heat gently over low heat while stirring for 3–4 minutes until agar dissolves. Do not boil. Step 2: Pour mixture into ramekins or glasses and refrigerate for at least 2 hours until set. Step 3: While panna cotta chills, peel and core the Asian pear, then slice thinly. Poach slices in a small saucepan with 100ml water and 1 tablespoon honey for 5–7 minutes until tender. Let cool. Step 4: Before serving, drizzle black sesame paste over each panna cotta and gently swirl with a toothpick. Top with poached pear slices and an extra drizzle of honey if desired.

menuItems.name: Sticky Rice with Mango
menuItems.description: Glutinous coconut sticky rice, fresh ripe mango slices, pandan leaf, sesame
menuItems.method: Step 1: Rinse glutinous rice until water runs clear, then soak for at least 30 minutes. Drain well. Step 2: In a saucepan, combine coconut milk, sugar, salt, and pandan leaves. Heat gently until sugar dissolves, then remove pandan leaves. Step 3: Steam the soaked rice for 15 minutes, then transfer to the coconut milk mixture. Stir well, cover, and let sit off heat for 10–15 minutes until liquid is absorbed and rice is tender. Step 4: Fluff the rice gently with a fork. Serve warm or at room temperature alongside fresh mango slices. Sprinkle with toasted sesame seeds just before serving for added aroma and crunch. The dish balances creamy sweetness with bright, tropical fruit—ideal as a dessert or light meal.

menuItems.name: Yuzu Cashew Cheesecake
menuItems.description: Vegan cashew cheesecake, yuzu curd, ginger biscuit crumble, matcha dusting
menuItems.method: Step 1: Soak raw cashews in hot water for 1 hour, then drain. Step 2: Blend soaked cashews with coconut cream, maple syrup, vanilla extract, and lemon zest until smooth and creamy. Step 3: Press crushed ginger biscuits mixed with melted vegan butter and agave nectar into a springform pan to form the base. Step 4: Pour cashew mixture over the base and smooth the top. Chill in the freezer for 2 hours. Step 5: Whisk yuzu juice with a bit of coconut cream and maple syrup to make a tangy curd; spoon gently over the set cheesecake. Step 6: Return to the fridge for 30 minutes to set. Before serving, dust lightly with matcha powder using a fine sieve for a vibrant green finish.

menuItems.name: Champion Chicken Breast
menuItems.description: Grilled 8oz chicken breast, sweet potato mash, steamed broccoli, lemon herb sauce
menuItems.method: Step 1: Season the chicken breast with salt, pepper, and 1 tbsp olive oil. Grill over medium-high heat for 6–7 minutes per side until internal temperature reaches 165°F. Rest for 5 minutes. Step 2: Peel and cube the sweet potato, then boil until tender (10–12 minutes). Drain, mash with butter or olive oil, and season to taste. Step 3: Steam broccoli florets for 4–5 minutes until bright green and crisp-tender. Step 4: Whisk together lemon juice, zest, remaining olive oil, garlic, parsley, thyme, salt, and pepper to make the herb sauce. Slice the grilled chicken and serve alongside sweet potato mash and steamed broccoli, drizzled with lemon herb sauce.

menuItems.name: Lean Beef Burger
menuItems.description: 6oz grass-fed beef patty, lettuce, tomato, onion, whole wheat bun, side salad
menuItems.method: Step 1: Gently shape the grass-fed ground beef into a 6-oz patty, season both sides with salt and pepper. Step 2: Heat a grill or skillet over medium-high heat; cook the patty for about 4 minutes per side for medium doneness, flipping once. Step 3: While the patty cooks, lightly toast the whole wheat bun. Step 4: Assemble the burger by placing the cooked patty on the bottom bun, then layering lettuce, tomato, and onion on top. Step 5: Add the top bun. Step 6: For the side salad, toss mixed greens with a drizzle of olive oil, a pinch of salt, and pepper. Serve immediately alongside the burger.

menuItems.name: Egg White Power Scramble
menuItems.description: 6 egg whites, spinach, mushrooms, bell peppers, turkey sausage, whole grain toast
menuItems.method: Step 1: In a nonstick skillet over medium heat, add the cooked turkey sausage and sauté for 1 minute to warm through. Step 2: Add the mushrooms and bell peppers, cooking for 3–4 minutes until softened. Step 3: Stir in the spinach and cook until wilted, about 1 minute. Step 4: In a bowl, whisk the egg whites lightly with a pinch of salt and pepper. Pour into the skillet over the vegetables and sausage. Step 5: Gently stir the egg whites as they cook, about 2–3 minutes, until fully set but still moist. Step 6: While the scramble cooks, toast the whole grain bread. Step 7: Serve the egg white scramble immediately alongside the toast for a high-protein, nutrient-rich breakfast.

menuItems.name: Tuna Poke Stack
menuItems.description: Fresh ahi tuna, avocado, cucumber, edamame, brown rice, spicy mayo
menuItems.method: Step 1: Cook brown rice according to package instructions and let cool slightly. Step 2: Dice the fresh ahi tuna into 1/2-inch cubes and gently fold in 2 tablespoons of spicy mayo. Step 3: Peel and dice the avocado, then toss lightly with a squeeze of lime juice to prevent browning. Step 4: If using frozen edamame, thaw and pat dry; dice cucumber into small pieces. Step 5: In serving bowls or glasses, layer brown rice at the bottom, followed by seasoned tuna, then a mix of avocado, cucumber, and edamame. Step 6: Drizzle remaining spicy mayo over the top and serve immediately, optionally garnished with sesame seeds or sliced green onions. Keep ingredients chilled until assembly for optimal freshness and texture.

menuItems.name: Protein Pancakes
menuItems.description: Whey protein pancakes, blueberries, Greek yogurt, maple syrup
menuItems.method: Step 1: In a blender, combine whey protein powder, egg whites, rolled oats, baking powder, and almond milk. Blend until smooth to form a thick batter. Step 2: Gently fold in fresh blueberries. Heat a non-stick skillet over medium heat and lightly grease with cooking spray. Pour 1/4 cup portions of batter onto the skillet and cook for 2–3 minutes per side, or until golden brown and cooked through. Step 3: Serve warm topped with Greek yogurt and a drizzle of pure maple syrup. Enjoy immediately for a high-protein, satisfying breakfast.

menuItems.name: Turkey & Quinoa Power Bowl
menuItems.description: Ground turkey, quinoa, roasted kale, cherry tomatoes, balsamic glaze
menuItems.method: Step 1: Cook quinoa according to package instructions using water or broth; set aside. Step 2: Preheat oven to 375°F (190°C). Toss chopped kale with 1 tablespoon olive oil, salt, and pepper; spread on a baking sheet and roast for 10–12 minutes until crisp. Step 3: In a skillet over medium heat, add remaining olive oil and cook ground turkey until browned and cooked through, about 6–8 minutes. Season with salt and pepper. Step 4: Assemble bowls by dividing cooked quinoa among serving bowls, then topping with roasted kale, cooked turkey, and halved cherry tomatoes. Drizzle each bowl with balsamic glaze. Serve warm or at room temperature.

menuItems.name: Salmon Fillet with Asparagus
menuItems.description: 6oz Atlantic salmon fillet, grilled asparagus, lemon butter, wild rice
menuItems.method: Step 1: Rinse wild rice and cook according to package instructions, typically simmering in water for 40–45 minutes until tender. Step 2: Preheat grill or grill pan over medium-high heat. Toss asparagus with olive oil, salt, and pepper; grill for 3–5 minutes until tender-crisp, turning occasionally. Step 3: Season salmon fillet with salt and pepper. Grill skin-side down for 4–5 minutes, then flip and cook another 2–3 minutes until just opaque. Step 4: While salmon rests, melt butter in a small saucepan over low heat. Stir in lemon zest and juice. Step 5: Plate wild rice, top with grilled asparagus and salmon, then drizzle with lemon butter sauce. Serve immediately.

menuItems.name: Steak & Egg Classic
menuItems.description: Sirloin steak, two eggs any style, hash browns, mixed greens
menuItems.method: Step 1: Season the sirloin steak generously with salt and pepper. Heat 1 tablespoon olive oil in a skillet over medium-high heat. Sear the steak for 4–5 minutes per side for medium-rare, then rest for 5 minutes before slicing. Step 2: While the steak rests, prepare hash browns by squeezing moisture from shredded potatoes, then fry in remaining oil until golden and crispy. Step 3: In the same pan, add butter and fry eggs to your preferred style—sunny-side up, over-easy, or scrambled. Step 4: Toss mixed greens with a pinch of salt and a drizzle of olive oil. Plate the sliced steak alongside hash browns, eggs, and greens. Serve immediately.

menuItems.name: Bone Broth Cup
menuItems.description: Slow-simmered beef bone broth, collagen-rich, sea salt, cracked pepper, fresh herbs
menuItems.method: Step 1: Place beef bones in a large pot and cover with cold water. Bring to a gentle boil, then reduce heat to low and skim off any impurities that rise to the surface. Step 2: Add sea salt, cracked pepper, thyme, and parsley. Simmer uncovered on very low heat for 12–24 hours, skimming occasionally to keep the broth clear. The longer it simmers, the more collagen and flavor will extract from the bones. Step 3: After simmering, strain the broth through a fine-mesh sieve into a clean container, discarding solids. Let cool slightly before serving warm in a mug or cup. Optionally, garnish with extra fresh herbs. Store leftovers in the refrigerator for up to 5 days or freeze for longer storage.

menuItems.name: Deviled Eggs with Turkey Bacon
menuItems.description: Six halved hard-boiled eggs, whipped yolk filling, crispy turkey bacon bits, paprika
menuItems.method: Step 1: Place eggs in a saucepan, cover with cold water, and bring to a boil. Once boiling, remove from heat, cover, and let sit for 10 minutes. Transfer to ice water to cool, then peel and halve lengthwise. Step 2: Carefully remove yolks and place in a bowl. Mash with mayonnaise, Dijon mustard, salt, and pepper until smooth. Step 3: Cook turkey bacon in a skillet over medium heat until crispy, about 5–7 minutes. Drain on paper towels, then crumble into small bits. Step 4: Spoon or pipe the yolk mixture back into the egg white halves. Top each with a sprinkle of crumbled turkey bacon and a light dusting of paprika. Chill for at least 15 minutes before serving for best flavor and texture.

menuItems.name: Buffalo Chicken Bites
menuItems.description: Crispy baked chicken bites, buffalo hot sauce, celery sticks, Greek yogurt ranch dip
menuItems.method: Step 1: Preheat oven to 425°F (220°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper. Cut chicken into 1-inch cubes. In a bowl, whisk flour, baking powder, salt, and pepper. Toss chicken in the mixture until evenly coated. Arrange on the baking sheet in a single layer. Step 2: Bake for 20–25 minutes, flipping halfway, until golden and cooked through. Meanwhile, melt butter and mix with buffalo sauce. Toss baked chicken in the sauce until fully coated. For the dip, combine Greek yogurt and ranch seasoning. Serve chicken bites hot with celery sticks and the Greek yogurt ranch dip on the side.

menuItems.name: Shrimp Cocktail
menuItems.description: Chilled jumbo shrimp, house cocktail sauce, fresh horseradish, lemon wedges
menuItems.method: Step 1: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Add the jumbo shrimp and cook for 2–3 minutes until pink and opaque. Immediately transfer to an ice bath to chill completely. Drain and pat dry. Step 2: In a small bowl, mix ketchup, fresh horseradish, lemon juice, Worcestershire sauce, and hot sauce to create the cocktail sauce. Taste and adjust seasoning if needed. Step 3: Arrange chilled shrimp on a serving platter or in individual glasses with tails curled outward. Serve with the house cocktail sauce in a small bowl or ramekin in the center and lemon wedges on the side. Keep refrigerated until ready to serve for optimal freshness and temperature.

menuItems.name: Greek Yogurt Parfait
menuItems.description: Thick Greek yogurt, mixed berries, house granola, honey drizzle, chia seeds
menuItems.method: Step 1: In a glass or bowl, spoon half of the Greek yogurt as the bottom layer. Step 2: Add half of the mixed berries on top of the yogurt, followed by half of the granola. Step 3: Repeat the layers with the remaining yogurt, berries, and granola. Step 4: Drizzle honey evenly over the top layer. Step 5: Sprinkle chia seeds across the surface for added texture and nutrition. Serve immediately or chill briefly for a cooler treat. This parfait combines creamy yogurt, tart-sweet berries, crunchy granola, and the subtle nuttiness of chia seeds, all enhanced by a touch of natural sweetness from honey. It’s a balanced, satisfying breakfast or snack that’s both visually appealing and nutrient-rich.

menuItems.name: Protein Brownie
menuItems.description: Dense chocolate brownie with whey protein and black beans, served warm with Greek yogurt
menuItems.method: Step 1: Preheat oven to 350°F (175°C) and grease an 8x8-inch baking pan. Step 2: In a food processor, blend the black beans until smooth. Add eggs, maple syrup (or honey), and vanilla; blend until combined. Step 3: Add whey protein powder, cocoa powder, baking powder, and salt. Pulse until fully incorporated and batter is thick but smooth. Step 4: Pour batter into the prepared pan and bake for 20–25 minutes, or until a toothpick inserted in the center comes out mostly clean (a few crumbs are fine). Step 5: Let cool slightly in the pan. Serve warm slices topped with a dollop of Greek yogurt for a creamy, high-protein contrast to the rich, fudgy brownie.

menuItems.name: Cottage Cheese Fruit Bowl
menuItems.description: Low-fat cottage cheese, fresh strawberries, pineapple chunks, kiwi, light honey
menuItems.method: Step 1: In a serving bowl, spoon the low-fat cottage cheese as the base. Step 2: Arrange the sliced strawberries, pineapple chunks, and kiwi evenly over the cottage cheese. Step 3: Drizzle the light honey gently over the fruit to add a touch of natural sweetness. Step 4: Serve immediately for the freshest flavor and texture, or chill for 10–15 minutes if preferred cold. This dish combines creamy protein with vibrant, vitamin-rich fruits for a balanced, refreshing snack or light breakfast. Avoid stirring too much to maintain distinct layers and textures. For extra zest, you may add a squeeze of lime or a sprinkle of chia seeds, though these are optional and not part of the original recipe.

menuItems.name: Peanut Butter Banana Nice Cream
menuItems.description: Frozen banana blended with natural peanut butter, topped with cacao nibs and hemp seeds
menuItems.method: Step 1: Peel and slice two ripe bananas, then freeze them for at least 4 hours or overnight until solid. Step 2: Add the frozen banana slices and 2 tablespoons of natural peanut butter to a high-speed blender or food processor. Blend on high, scraping down the sides as needed, until the mixture becomes creamy and smooth—this usually takes 1–2 minutes. Step 3: Once the nice cream reaches a soft-serve consistency, transfer it to a serving bowl or dish. Step 4: Sprinkle evenly with 1 tablespoon of cacao nibs and 1 tablespoon of hemp seeds for added crunch, healthy fats, and antioxidants. Serve immediately for a soft texture, or freeze for 15–20 minutes if a firmer consistency is preferred. Enjoy this dairy-free, naturally sweetened dessert right away!

menuItems.name: Margherita Pizza
menuItems.description: San Marzano tomatoes, fresh mozzarella, basil, extra virgin olive oil, wood-fired crust
menuItems.method: Step 1: Preheat a wood-fired oven (or conventional oven at highest setting with a pizza stone) to 500°F (260°C). Step 2: Roll out the pizza dough on a floured surface into a 12-inch circle. Step 3: Spread crushed San Marzano tomatoes evenly over the dough, leaving a small border for the crust. Season lightly with salt and pepper if desired. Step 4: Distribute mozzarella pieces evenly across the sauce. Step 5: Drizzle with extra virgin olive oil. Step 6: Transfer the pizza to the hot oven and bake for 8–10 minutes until the crust is blistered and golden and the cheese is melted and bubbly. Step 7: Remove from oven, top immediately with fresh basil leaves, and drizzle with a touch more olive oil before serving.

menuItems.name: Cacio e Pepe
menuItems.description: Tonnarelli pasta, Pecorino Romano, black pepper, butter
menuItems.method: Step 1: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil and cook the tonnarelli according to package instructions until al dente. Reserve about 1 cup of pasta water before draining. Step 2: While the pasta cooks, toast the black pepper in a dry skillet over medium heat for 1–2 minutes until fragrant. Remove from heat and set aside. Step 3: In a large bowl, combine the grated Pecorino Romano with a splash of reserved pasta water to form a creamy paste. Step 4: Add the drained hot pasta to the bowl and toss vigorously, gradually adding more pasta water as needed to emulsify the sauce. Step 5: Stir in the toasted black pepper and butter, mixing until glossy and well-coated. Serve immediately with extra Pecorino and pepper on top if desired.

menuItems.name: Seafood Linguine
menuItems.description: Linguine, shrimp, clams, mussels, cherry tomatoes, white wine, garlic
menuItems.method: Step 1: Cook linguine in salted boiling water until al dente; reserve 1/2 cup pasta water and drain. Step 2: In a large skillet, heat olive oil over medium heat. Add garlic and sauté until fragrant, about 1 minute. Step 3: Add clams and mussels, then pour in white wine. Cover and steam for 5–6 minutes until shells open; discard any unopened shells. Step 4: Stir in shrimp and cherry tomatoes; cook 3–4 minutes until shrimp turn pink and tomatoes soften. Step 5: Add cooked linguine and toss to combine, adding reserved pasta water as needed to loosen the sauce. Season with salt and pepper. Garnish with parsley if desired and serve immediately.

menuItems.name: Tiramisu
menuItems.description: Ladyfingers, mascarpone cream, espresso, cocoa powder, Marsala wine
menuItems.method: Step 1: Separate egg yolks and whites. Whisk yolks with sugar until pale and creamy, then fold in mascarpone until smooth. In a separate bowl, beat egg whites to stiff peaks and gently fold into the mascarpone mixture. Step 2: Combine cooled espresso and Marsala wine in a shallow dish. Quickly dip each ladyfinger into the coffee mixture (do not soak) and layer them in a rectangular dish. Spread half the mascarpone cream over the ladyfingers. Repeat with another layer of dipped ladyfingers and remaining cream. Step 3: Cover and refrigerate for at least 4 hours or overnight. Before serving, dust the top evenly with cocoa powder using a fine sieve.

menuItems.name: Burrata & Prosciutto
menuItems.description: Fresh burrata, thinly sliced prosciutto, arugula, balsamic reduction, grilled bread
menuItems.method: Step 1: Preheat a grill pan or skillet over medium-high heat. Lightly brush both sides of the bread slices with olive oil and grill until golden and crisp, about 1–2 minutes per side. Set aside to cool slightly. Step 2: Arrange the arugula on a serving plate. Tear or place the burrata gently in the center. Drape the prosciutto slices around or over the burrata. Drizzle the balsamic reduction evenly over the top. Finish with a sprinkle of freshly cracked black pepper and a pinch of flaky sea salt if desired. Serve immediately with the grilled bread on the side for spreading or scooping. This dish is best enjoyed fresh and at room temperature to fully appreciate the creamy texture of the burrata and the savory richness of the prosciutto.

menuItems.name: Ribollita
menuItems.description: Tuscan bread soup with cannellini beans, kale, carrots, rosemary
menuItems.method: Step 1: Heat olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add onion, carrots, and celery; sauté until softened, about 8 minutes. Stir in garlic and rosemary; cook for 1 minute. Step 2: Add crushed tomatoes, kale, cannellini beans, and vegetable broth. Bring to a simmer and cook for 20–25 minutes until vegetables are tender. Season with salt and pepper. Step 3: Stir in torn stale bread and simmer for another 10–15 minutes until the soup thickens. Traditionally, ribollita is refrigerated overnight and reheated the next day ('ribollita' means 'reboiled'), which enhances flavor and texture. Serve warm with a drizzle of olive oil.

menuItems.name: Osso Buco
menuItems.description: Braised veal shank, gremolata, saffron risotto, slow-cooked in white wine
menuItems.method: Step 1: Season veal shanks with salt and pepper, then dredge in flour. Sear in olive oil until golden brown; set aside. Step 2: In the same pot, sauté onion, carrot, and celery until soft. Add garlic and cook briefly. Deglaze with white wine, scraping up browned bits. Return shanks to pot, add stock, tomatoes, and bay leaf. Simmer covered for 1.5–2 hours until tender. Step 3: Meanwhile, prepare gremolata by mixing parsley, lemon zest, and minced garlic. For saffron risotto, steep saffron in warm stock. Sauté rice in butter until translucent, then gradually add saffron-infused stock, stirring until creamy. Finish with Parmesan. Step 4: Serve osso buco over risotto, topped with gremolata.

menuItems.name: Pesto Gnocchi
menuItems.description: Potato gnocchi, basil pesto, cherry tomatoes, pine nuts, Parmesan
menuItems.method: Step 1: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Add the potato gnocchi and cook according to package instructions until they float to the surface, about 2–3 minutes. Drain and set aside, reserving 1/4 cup of pasta water. Step 2: In a large skillet over medium heat, gently warm the basil pesto. Add the cooked gnocchi and toss to coat evenly, adding a splash of reserved pasta water if needed to loosen the sauce. Step 3: Fold in the halved cherry tomatoes and cook for 1–2 minutes until just softened. Step 4: Remove from heat, stir in toasted pine nuts, and transfer to serving plates. Top generously with freshly grated Parmesan cheese. Serve immediately while warm.

menuItems.name: Carpaccio di Manzo
menuItems.description: Thinly sliced raw beef tenderloin, rocket, Parmesan shavings, capers, truffle oil
menuItems.method: Step 1: Freeze the beef tenderloin for 30–60 minutes to firm it up, then slice paper-thin using a sharp knife or meat slicer. Arrange the slices evenly on a chilled plate, slightly overlapping. Step 2: In a small bowl, whisk together olive oil, lemon juice, salt, and pepper. Drizzle lightly over the beef. Step 3: Scatter fresh rocket leaves over the beef, followed by Parmesan shavings and capers. Finish with a delicate drizzle of truffle oil. Serve immediately, ensuring all ingredients are cold and fresh for optimal flavor and texture.

menuItems.name: Bruschetta al Pomodoro
menuItems.description: Toasted sourdough, ripe San Marzano tomatoes, fresh basil, garlic, extra virgin olive oil
menuItems.method: Step 1: Preheat a grill or skillet over medium heat. Lightly toast the sourdough slices until golden and crisp on both sides. While still warm, rub one side of each slice with a peeled garlic clove. Step 2: In a bowl, combine the diced San Marzano tomatoes, chopped basil, 2 tablespoons of olive oil, salt, and pepper. Let the mixture sit for 5–10 minutes to allow flavors to meld. Step 3: Spoon the tomato mixture generously onto the garlic-rubbed side of each toasted slice. Drizzle with the remaining olive oil just before serving. Serve immediately while the bread is still crisp and the tomatoes are fresh and juicy.

menuItems.name: Fritto Misto
menuItems.description: Lightly battered calamari, shrimp, zucchini flowers, lemon aioli
menuItems.method: Step 1: Prepare lemon aioli by mixing mayonnaise, minced garlic, lemon juice, and a pinch of salt; refrigerate until serving. Step 2: Gently rinse zucchini flowers and pat dry, removing stamens if present. Pat seafood dry with paper towels. Step 3: In a bowl, whisk flour, salt, and ice-cold sparkling water until just combined—do not overmix; small lumps are fine. Keep batter cold. Step 4: Heat oil in a deep fryer or pot to 180°C (350°F). Dip ingredients one at a time into the batter, letting excess drip off, then fry in batches until golden and crisp (about 2–3 minutes). Avoid overcrowding. Step 5: Drain on paper towels, season lightly with salt, and serve immediately with lemon wedges and lemon aioli.

menuItems.name: Insalata Caprese
menuItems.description: Buffalo mozzarella, heirloom tomatoes, fresh basil, aged balsamic, sea salt
menuItems.method: Step 1: Slice the buffalo mozzarella and heirloom tomatoes into 1/4-inch thick rounds. Step 2: Arrange alternating slices of tomato and mozzarella on a serving platter, slightly overlapping them in a circular or linear pattern. Step 3: Tuck fresh basil leaves between each slice or scatter them evenly over the top. Step 4: Drizzle the aged balsamic vinegar generously over the arranged salad. Step 5: Sprinkle sea salt lightly across the surface to enhance the flavors. Allow the salad to sit at room temperature for about 10 minutes before serving to let the ingredients meld. Serve immediately as a light appetizer or side dish. Do not refrigerate beforehand, as cold temperatures dull the flavor of the tomatoes and cheese.

menuItems.name: Panna Cotta al Limoncello
menuItems.description: Creamy vanilla panna cotta, limoncello syrup, candied lemon zest, fresh mint
menuItems.method: Step 1: Bloom gelatin by sprinkling it over cold water and let sit for 5 minutes. Step 2: In a saucepan, combine cream, milk, sugar, and split vanilla bean (or extract). Heat gently until sugar dissolves and mixture is warm—do not boil. Step 3: Remove from heat, stir in bloomed gelatin until fully dissolved. Strain into ramekins and chill for at least 4 hours or until set. Step 4: For syrup, simmer limoncello with a tablespoon of sugar until slightly thickened; cool. Step 5: For candied zest, blanch lemon strips in boiling water twice, then simmer in simple syrup until translucent; dry on parchment. Step 6: Unmold panna cotta onto plates, drizzle with limoncello syrup, top with candied zest and fresh mint.

menuItems.name: Cannoli Siciliani
menuItems.description: Crispy pastry shells filled with sweet ricotta cream, candied orange peel, pistachios
menuItems.method: Step 1: In a large bowl, combine the drained ricotta cheese, powdered sugar, and vanilla extract. Mix until smooth and creamy; refrigerate for at least 1 hour to firm up and enhance flavor. Step 2: Just before serving, gently fold in the chopped candied orange peel, pistachios, and optional mini chocolate chips. Step 3: Using a piping bag fitted with a wide tip, carefully fill each cannoli shell from both ends to ensure even distribution and avoid sogginess. Step 4: Dust filled cannoli lightly with additional powdered sugar if desired, and garnish with extra chopped pistachios on the ends. Serve immediately for optimal crispness. Do not fill shells too far in advance, as moisture from the filling softens the pastry.

menuItems.name: Affogato al CaffÃ¨
menuItems.description: Vanilla gelato drowned in a double shot of hot espresso, amaretti biscuit

menuItems.name: Torta della Nonna
menuItems.description: Traditional Italian custard tart, pine nuts, lemon zest, icing sugar dusting
menuItems.method: Step 1: Preheat oven to 350°F (180°C). Roll out shortcrust pastry and line a 9-inch tart pan; prick base with a fork and blind bake for 15 minutes until lightly golden. Step 2: Meanwhile, heat milk with lemon zest until steaming. Whisk egg yolks and sugar until pale, then blend in flour. Slowly pour hot milk into yolk mixture while whisking. Return mixture to saucepan and cook over medium heat, stirring constantly, until thickened (about 3–5 minutes). Remove from heat; stir in vanilla. Step 3: Pour warm custard into pre-baked crust. Sprinkle pine nuts evenly over the top. Bake for 20–25 minutes until pine nuts are golden. Cool completely, then dust generously with icing sugar before serving.

menuItems.name: Tonkotsu Ramen
menuItems.description: Rich pork bone broth, chashu pork belly, soft-boiled egg, nori, bamboo shoots
menuItems.method: Step 1: Simmer pork bones in water for 12–18 hours, skimming impurities, until broth is creamy and rich. Add smashed garlic and ginger during the last hour. Step 2: Meanwhile, roll and tie pork belly, then braise in soy sauce, mirin, sake, and water for 2–3 hours until tender; slice thinly. Step 3: Soft-boil eggs for 6–7 minutes, chill in ice water, peel, and marinate in soy-mirin mixture overnight. Step 4: Cook ramen noodles according to package instructions. Step 5: Assemble bowls: ladle hot broth over noodles, top with sliced chashu, halved marinated egg, nori, drained bamboo shoots, and finely chopped green onions. Serve immediately.

menuItems.name: Shoyu Ramen
menuItems.description: Soy-based broth, chicken chashu, menma, narutomaki, green onions
menuItems.method: Step 1: In a pot, combine chicken broth, soy sauce, mirin, minced garlic, and grated ginger. Simmer gently for 15 minutes to meld flavors. Step 2: Meanwhile, cook ramen noodles according to package instructions until al dente; drain and rinse briefly under warm water. Step 3: Reheat the sliced chicken chashu in a pan or microwave until warm. Step 4: Divide noodles between two bowls and ladle the hot shoyu broth over them. Step 5: Arrange chicken chashu, menma, and narutomaki slices on top. Step 6: Garnish generously with chopped green onions. Serve immediately while hot.

menuItems.name: Vegan Miso Ramen
menuItems.description: White miso broth, tofu, corn, bok choy, sesame, mushrooms
menuItems.method: Step 1: Heat sesame oil in a pot over medium heat. Add sliced shiitake mushrooms and sauté until tender, about 5 minutes. Step 2: Add vegetable broth and bring to a gentle simmer. In a small bowl, whisk white miso paste with a ladle of hot broth until smooth, then stir back into the pot. Do not boil after adding miso to preserve flavor and probiotics. Step 3: Meanwhile, cook ramen noodles according to package instructions; drain and set aside. Cube tofu and pan-fry until golden. Blanch bok choy in boiling water for 1–2 minutes. Step 4: Assemble bowls with noodles, tofu, bok choy, and corn. Ladle hot miso broth over top. Garnish with sesame seeds and green onions.

menuItems.name: Gyoza (6 pcs)
menuItems.description: Pan-fried pork and cabbage dumplings, ponzu dipping sauce
menuItems.method: Step 1: In a bowl, combine ground pork, chopped cabbage (salted and squeezed dry), green onions, garlic, ginger, soy sauce, and sesame oil. Mix well until sticky. Step 2: Place about 1 tbsp of filling in the center of each gyoza wrapper. Fold and pleat edges to seal tightly. Step 3: Heat vegetable oil in a non-stick pan over medium heat. Arrange dumplings flat-side down and fry until golden brown (2–3 minutes). Step 4: Add water to the pan, immediately cover, and steam for 5–6 minutes until wrappers are translucent and filling is cooked through. Step 5: Uncover, let excess water evaporate, then serve hot with ponzu dipping sauce.

menuItems.name: Spicy Tantanmen
menuItems.description: Sesame broth, chili oil, minced pork, bok choy, pickled mustard greens
menuItems.method: Step 1: Cook ramen noodles according to package instructions; set aside. Step 2: In a pot, heat a bit of chili oil over medium heat. Add garlic and ginger, sauté until fragrant. Add ground pork and cook until browned. Step 3: Stir in sesame paste, soy sauce, rice vinegar, and broth. Simmer for 10 minutes to develop flavor. Step 4: Blanch bok choy in boiling water for 1–2 minutes until tender-crisp. Step 5: Divide cooked noodles into bowls. Ladle hot sesame-chili broth over noodles. Top with cooked pork mixture, bok choy, and pickled mustard greens. Step 6: Garnish with sliced green onions and toasted sesame seeds. Adjust chili oil to taste for desired heat level.

menuItems.name: Karaage Chicken
menuItems.description: Japanese fried chicken, yuzu mayo, pickled ginger, shredded cabbage
menuItems.method: Step 1: Cut chicken thighs into bite-sized pieces. Marinate in soy sauce, sake, grated ginger, and minced garlic for at least 30 minutes. Step 2: Drain excess marinade, then coat chicken thoroughly in cornstarch. Heat vegetable oil to 170°C (340°F) and fry chicken in batches until golden brown and cooked through, about 5–6 minutes. Drain on paper towels. Step 3: Mix mayonnaise with yuzu juice to make yuzu mayo. Serve karaage hot with shredded cabbage as a bed, topped with pickled ginger, and drizzle or serve yuzu mayo on the side. Ensure chicken is crispy outside and juicy inside.

menuItems.name: Matcha Ice Cream
menuItems.description: House-made matcha green tea ice cream, red bean paste, mochi
menuItems.method: Step 1: Whisk matcha powder with a small amount of warm milk until smooth. Set aside. Step 2: In a saucepan, heat the remaining milk and heavy cream until steaming but not boiling. Step 3: In a bowl, whisk egg yolks and sugar until pale, then slowly temper in the hot cream mixture. Return to the pan and cook over medium heat, stirring constantly, until it thickens enough to coat the back of a spoon. Step 4: Remove from heat, stir in the matcha mixture, then strain and chill thoroughly. Step 5: Churn in an ice cream maker according to manufacturer’s instructions. Step 6: During the last minute of churning, add red bean paste and mochi pieces. Transfer to a container and freeze until firm, about 4 hours.

menuItems.name: Chashu Rice Bowl
menuItems.description: Braised pork belly slices, steamed rice, soft-boiled egg, pickled cucumber
menuItems.method: Step 1: Place eggs in boiling water for 6–7 minutes, then chill in ice water; peel and set aside. Step 2: In a pot, combine soy sauce, mirin, sake, brown sugar, and enough water to cover pork belly. Bring to a simmer. Step 3: Add pork belly, skin-side up, and braise on low heat for 1.5–2 hours until tender. Let cool in braising liquid, then slice thinly. Step 4: Thinly slice cucumber, toss with rice vinegar, salt, and a pinch of sugar; let sit 10 minutes. Step 5: Reheat sliced chashu briefly if needed. Step 6: Assemble bowls with steamed rice, top with chashu slices, halved soft-boiled egg, and pickled cucumber. Drizzle with a spoonful of braising liquid if desired.

menuItems.name: Agedashi Tofu
menuItems.description: Lightly battered silken tofu, dashi broth, grated daikon, bonito flakes, scallions
menuItems.method: Step 1: Drain silken tofu and cut into 1.5-inch cubes. Pat dry gently with paper towels. Step 2: Heat vegetable oil to 350°F (175°C). Lightly coat tofu cubes in potato starch, shaking off excess. Fry until golden and crisp, about 2–3 minutes. Drain on paper towels. Step 3: In a small saucepan, combine dashi, soy sauce, and mirin. Warm gently without boiling. Step 4: Place fried tofu in serving bowls. Pour warm broth over tofu. Top with grated daikon, bonito flakes, and chopped scallions. Serve immediately while tofu is crisp and broth is hot.

menuItems.name: Takoyaki (6 pcs)
menuItems.description: Grilled octopus balls, okonomiyaki sauce, Japanese mayo, bonito flakes, nori

ingredients.name: takoyaki batter (made from flour, dashi, egg, and green onion)

menuItems.method: Step 1: Preheat a takoyaki pan over medium heat and lightly oil the hemispherical molds. Pour batter into each mold until three-quarters full. Step 2: Add one piece of octopus, a few tempura scraps, and a pinch of pickled ginger to each mold. As the edges begin to set, use a skewer or pick to rotate the balls every 30–60 seconds, shaping them into spheres as they cook through—about 5–7 minutes total. Step 3: Once golden brown and crisp, transfer to a serving plate. Drizzle with okonomiyaki sauce and Japanese mayo. Top generously with bonito flakes and sprinkle with shredded nori. Serve immediately while hot and crispy.

menuItems.name: Edamame Shio
menuItems.description: Steamed edamame pods finished with sea salt and yuzu kosho
menuItems.method: Step 1: If using frozen edamame, there’s no need to thaw. Bring a pot of water to a boil and add the edamame pods. Boil for 4–5 minutes until bright green and tender. Step 2: Drain the edamame thoroughly and transfer to a serving bowl. While still warm, sprinkle evenly with sea salt and gently toss to coat. Step 3: Add yuzu kosho—a citrusy, spicy Japanese condiment—and mix lightly to distribute its flavor without overpowering the beans. Serve immediately while warm, ideally with a small dish on the side for discarded pods. This simple preparation highlights the natural sweetness of edamame, enhanced by the briny crunch of sea salt and the aromatic heat of yuzu kosho. Enjoy as a snack, appetizer, or side dish with beer or sake.

menuItems.name: Spicy Chicken Karaage Skewers
menuItems.description: Marinated crispy chicken thigh skewers, shiso tare, togarashi, pickled cucumber
menuItems.method: Step 1: Soak bamboo skewers in water for 30 minutes. Cut chicken thighs into 1-inch cubes and marinate in soy sauce, sake, ginger, and garlic for at least 30 minutes. Step 2: Drain chicken, pat dry, then toss with cornstarch until evenly coated. Heat oil to 170°C (340°F) and fry chicken in batches until golden and crispy, about 3–4 minutes. Drain on paper towels. Step 3: Thread fried chicken onto skewers. For shiso tare, finely chop shiso leaves and mix with rice vinegar, mirin, and a pinch of togarashi. Brush lightly over skewers or serve as dipping sauce. Step 4: Toss cucumber slices with salt, let sit 5 minutes, then rinse and drain for quick pickles. Serve skewers with pickled cucumber and extra togarashi for heat.

menuItems.name: Dorayaki
menuItems.description: Soft Japanese pancake sandwich filled with sweet red bean paste and whipped cream
menuItems.method: Step 1: In a bowl, whisk together flour and baking powder. In another bowl, beat egg and sugar until pale, then add honey and milk; mix well. Gradually fold dry ingredients into wet until smooth. Rest batter 15 minutes. Step 2: Heat a lightly greased nonstick pan over medium-low heat. Pour small rounds of batter (about 3 inches wide) and cook until bubbles form, then flip and cook other side until golden. Cool completely. Step 3: Whip heavy cream with powdered sugar until soft peaks form. Spread a layer of whipped cream on one pancake, top with red bean paste, then cap with another pancake. Repeat for remaining pancakes. Serve immediately or chill briefly before serving.

menuItems.name: Warabi Mochi
menuItems.description: Bracken-starch mochi dusted with kinako and drizzled with black sugar syrup
menuItems.method: Step 1: In a saucepan, mix warabi starch with water until fully dissolved. Heat over medium heat, stirring constantly, until the mixture thickens and becomes translucent and jelly-like (about 5–7 minutes). Step 2: Pour the mixture into a shallow dish lined with plastic wrap or lightly oiled, spreading evenly. Let cool to room temperature, then refrigerate for at least 2 hours until firm. Step 3: Once set, cut the chilled mochi into bite-sized cubes or rectangles. Step 4: Place kinako in a shallow bowl and gently roll each piece of mochi to coat thoroughly. Step 5: Arrange coated mochi on a serving plate and drizzle generously with kuromitsu just before serving. Serve chilled for a refreshing, chewy dessert with nutty and sweet flavors.

menuItems.name: Taiyaki
menuItems.description: Fish-shaped waffle filled with sweet azuki red bean paste, served warm
menuItems.method: Step 1: In a bowl, whisk together flour, baking powder, and sugar. In another bowl, beat the egg, then add milk and oil; mix well. Gradually combine wet ingredients into dry ingredients until smooth. Step 2: Preheat a taiyaki or fish-shaped waffle iron and lightly grease it. Pour a small amount of batter to cover the bottom half of each mold. Add about 1 teaspoon of red bean paste in the center. Cover with more batter to fill the mold. Step 3: Close the iron and cook for 3–4 minutes until golden brown and cooked through. Carefully remove and serve warm. Repeat with remaining batter and filling. Ensure even cooking by adjusting heat as needed.

menuItems.name: Hojicha Ice Cream
menuItems.description: House-made roasted green tea ice cream, toasted rice puff, sesame brittle
menuItems.method: Step 1: Whisk egg yolks and sugar until pale. Heat milk and hojicha powder in a saucepan until steaming; gradually temper into yolk mixture. Return to pan and cook over medium heat, stirring constantly, until thick enough to coat the back of a spoon. Step 2: Strain custard into a bowl, then stir in heavy cream. Chill thoroughly (at least 4 hours or overnight). Churn in an ice cream maker according to manufacturer’s instructions. In the last minute of churning, add toasted rice puffs. Transfer to a freezer-safe container, layering with crushed sesame brittle as you go. Freeze until firm, about 4–6 hours. Serve scoops garnished with extra brittle and rice puffs for texture and visual appeal.

menuItems.name: Carne Asada Tacos
menuItems.description: Three grilled flank steak tacos, pico de gallo, guacamole, cilantro, corn tortillas
menuItems.method: Step 1: Marinate the flank steak in lime juice, olive oil, salt, and pepper for at least 30 minutes. Step 2: Heat a grill or skillet over high heat and cook the steak for 4–5 minutes per side for medium-rare. Let it rest for 5 minutes, then slice thinly against the grain. Step 3: Warm the corn tortillas on the grill or in a dry skillet until pliable. Step 4: Assemble the tacos by placing slices of grilled steak onto each tortilla. Top with pico de gallo, guacamole, and fresh chopped cilantro. Serve immediately with extra lime wedges if desired. This yields three generous tacos with bold, fresh flavors typical of authentic street-style carne asada.

menuItems.name: Veggie Burrito Bowl
menuItems.description: Black beans, roasted peppers, corn, guacamole, brown rice, pico de gallo, lime crema

ingredients.name: lime crema
ingredients.amount: 2 tablespoons (mix sour cream or Greek yogurt with lime juice and zest)

menuItems.method: Step 1: Prepare brown rice according to package instructions and let cool slightly. Step 2: In a small bowl, warm black beans with a pinch of salt and optional cumin; set aside. Step 3: If using raw corn, lightly sauté or grill until tender; otherwise, use thawed frozen or canned corn. Step 4: Assemble the bowl by placing a base of brown rice at the bottom. Step 5: Arrange black beans, roasted peppers, and corn in sections over the rice. Step 6: Add a generous spoonful of guacamole and pico de gallo on top. Step 7: Drizzle with lime crema. Step 8: Serve immediately with lime wedges on the side for extra brightness. Customize with cilantro or hot sauce if desired.

menuItems.name: Chicken Enchiladas
menuItems.description: Corn tortillas stuffed with shredded chicken, red chili sauce, melted cheese, sour cream

ingredients.name: shredded cheese (e.g., Monterey Jack or cheddar)

menuItems.method: Step 1: Preheat oven to 350°F (175°C). Lightly grease a 9x13-inch baking dish. Step 2: Warm corn tortillas in a dry skillet or microwave until pliable; lightly fry each in vegetable oil for 10 seconds per side to soften and prevent cracking. Step 3: Dip each tortilla in warm red chili sauce, then fill with shredded chicken and a sprinkle of cheese. Roll tightly and place seam-side down in the baking dish. Step 4: Pour remaining red chili sauce over enchiladas, then top with remaining cheese. Step 5: Bake uncovered for 20–25 minutes until bubbly and cheese is melted. Step 6: Let cool slightly, then drizzle with sour cream before serving. Optional: garnish with chopped cilantro or onion.

menuItems.name: Guacamole & Chips
menuItems.description: Fresh avocado, lime, cilantro, jalapeÃ±o, tomato, tortilla chips
menuItems.method: Step 1: Cut the avocados in half, remove the pits, and scoop the flesh into a bowl. Mash with a fork until mostly smooth but slightly chunky. Step 2: Add lime juice immediately to prevent browning and enhance flavor. Stir in chopped cilantro, diced jalapeño, and tomato. Season with salt to taste and mix gently to combine. Taste and adjust seasoning or lime as needed. Serve immediately with tortilla chips for dipping. For best results, use ripe but firm avocados and fresh ingredients. If preparing ahead, press plastic wrap directly onto the surface of the guacamole to minimize air exposure and refrigerate until ready to serve.

menuItems.name: Fish Tacos Baja Style
menuItems.description: Beer-battered cod, cabbage slaw, chipotle sauce, pickled red onion, flour tortillas
menuItems.method: Step 1: Prepare pickled red onions by combining sliced red onion, white vinegar, sugar, and a pinch of salt; let sit for at least 30 minutes. Step 2: Make chipotle sauce by mixing mayonnaise with chipotle in adobo until smooth; refrigerate until use. Step 3: Whisk beer and flour with a pinch of salt to form a batter. Dip cod pieces into the batter. Step 4: Heat oil in a deep pan and fry battered cod until golden and cooked through, about 3–4 minutes per side. Drain on paper towels. Step 5: Warm tortillas. Assemble tacos with fried cod, shredded cabbage, pickled onions, and chipotle sauce. Serve with lime wedges.

menuItems.name: Quesadilla de Hongos
menuItems.description: Mushroom and cheese quesadilla, salsa verde, sour cream, cilantro

ingredients.name: Mixed mushrooms (such as cremini, shiitake, and oyster)

menuItems.method: Step 1: Heat olive oil or butter in a skillet over medium heat. Sauté onions until translucent, then add garlic and mushrooms. Cook until mushrooms are tender and browned, about 5–7 minutes. Season with salt and pepper. Step 2: Place two tortillas on a clean surface. Divide the mushroom mixture evenly between them, then top with shredded cheese. Cover each with another tortilla. Step 3: Heat a dry skillet or griddle over medium heat. Cook each quesadilla for 2–3 minutes per side, until golden brown and cheese is melted. Step 4: Cut into wedges and serve immediately with salsa verde, a dollop of sour cream, and fresh cilantro sprinkled on top.

menuItems.name: Churros con Chocolate
menuItems.description: Crispy churros, dark chocolate dipping sauce, cinnamon sugar
menuItems.method: Step 1: In a saucepan, combine water, butter, sugar, and salt; bring to a boil. Remove from heat and stir in flour until smooth. Let cool slightly, then beat in eggs one at a time until glossy. Step 2: Heat oil to 375°F (190°C). Pipe 4–6 inch strips of dough into hot oil using a star tip, cutting with scissors. Fry until golden brown, about 2 minutes per side. Drain on paper towels. Step 3: Mix cinnamon and sugar; roll warm churros in mixture. Step 4: For the sauce, heat cream until simmering, pour over chopped chocolate, let sit 2 minutes, then stir until smooth. Serve churros immediately with warm chocolate dipping sauce.

menuItems.name: Pozole Rojo
menuItems.description: Traditional red pork and hominy soup, shredded cabbage, radish, lime, oregano
menuItems.method: Step 1: Simmer pork shoulder in water or broth with half the onion, 2 garlic cloves, bay leaves, and salt until tender (about 1.5 hours). Remove meat, shred, and set aside. Step 2: Toast guajillo and ancho chiles in a dry skillet until fragrant. Soak in hot water for 20 minutes, then blend with remaining onion, garlic, cumin, and oregano into a smooth paste. Strain and add to the broth. Step 3: Add hominy and shredded pork to the broth; simmer for 30–45 minutes. Adjust seasoning. Step 4: Serve hot, topped with shredded cabbage, radish slices, extra oregano, and lime wedges on the side for squeezing.

menuItems.name: Elote Street Corn
menuItems.description: Grilled corn cob, crema, cotija cheese, chili powder, lime, fresh cilantro
menuItems.method: Step 1: Preheat a grill to medium-high heat. Peel back the husks of the corn (without removing them completely), remove the silk, and then pull the husks back up around the corn. Soak the corn in cold water for 10 minutes. Step 2: Grill the corn, turning occasionally, for 10–15 minutes until kernels are tender and slightly charred. Remove husks and let cool slightly. Step 3: In a small bowl, mix crema with a squeeze of lime juice. Brush this mixture generously over each grilled ear. Step 4: Sprinkle cotija cheese evenly over the corn, followed by chili powder and chopped cilantro. Serve immediately with extra lime wedges for squeezing. Enjoy this classic Mexican street snack hot off the grill!

menuItems.name: Queso Fundido
menuItems.description: Melted Oaxacan cheese with chorizo and roasted peppers, served with warm flour tortillas
menuItems.method: Step 1: Remove the casing from the chorizo and cook it in a skillet over medium heat until browned and cooked through, about 5–7 minutes. Drain excess grease if needed. Step 2: Preheat your oven to 375°F (190°C). In an oven-safe skillet or baking dish, layer half the Oaxacan cheese, followed by the cooked chorizo and roasted poblano peppers. Top with the remaining cheese. Step 3: Bake for 10–12 minutes, or until the cheese is fully melted and bubbling. Alternatively, broil for 3–5 minutes, watching closely to prevent burning. Step 4: Remove from the oven and let cool slightly. Serve immediately with warm flour tortillas on the side for scooping or wrapping. Garnish with chopped cilantro or a squeeze of lime if desired.

menuItems.name: Ceviche de CamarÃ³n
menuItems.description: Fresh shrimp cured in lime juice, tomato, cucumber, red onion, jalapeÃ±o, cilantro, tostadas

menuItems.name: Sopa de Tortilla
menuItems.description: Ancho chili tomato broth, crispy tortilla strips, avocado, sour cream, Cotija cheese
menuItems.method: Step 1: Toast the dried ancho chilies in a dry skillet until fragrant, then soak in hot water for 15 minutes. Blend with roasted tomatoes, garlic, and onion until smooth. Step 2: Heat oil in a pot, sauté a bit of onion, then add the chili-tomato puree and cook for 5 minutes. Add broth and simmer for 20 minutes; season with salt. Step 3: Cut tortillas into strips, fry in oil until crispy, and drain on paper towels. Step 4: Ladle hot soup into bowls, top with crispy tortilla strips, diced avocado, a dollop of sour cream, and crumbled Cotija cheese. Serve immediately.

menuItems.name: Tres Leches Cake
menuItems.description: Light sponge soaked in three milks, whipped cream, cinnamon, fresh strawberries
menuItems.method: Step 1: Preheat oven to 350°F (175°C). Grease and flour a 9x13-inch baking pan. Sift together flour, baking powder, and salt. Step 2: Beat eggs and sugar until thick and pale, about 5 minutes. Gently fold in vanilla and milk, then the dry ingredients until just combined. Pour into pan and bake 25–30 minutes until golden and springy. Let cool completely. Step 3: Pierce cake all over with a fork. Combine sweetened condensed milk, evaporated milk, and whole milk; slowly pour over cake. Refrigerate at least 4 hours or overnight. Step 4: Whip heavy cream with cinnamon until stiff peaks form. Spread over soaked cake and top with fresh strawberries before serving.

menuItems.name: Flan de Vainilla
menuItems.description: Classic Mexican vanilla flan with burnt caramel sauce, fresh orange zest
menuItems.method: Step 1: Preheat oven to 350°F (175°C). In a small saucepan over medium heat, melt 1/2 cup sugar until it turns deep amber; immediately pour into a 9-inch round baking dish, swirling to coat the bottom. Step 2: In a blender, combine eggs, 3/4 cup sugar, condensed milk, evaporated milk, whole milk, vanilla, and orange zest. Blend until smooth. Pour mixture over cooled caramel in the dish. Step 3: Place the dish in a larger roasting pan; fill the outer pan with hot water halfway up the sides of the flan dish. Bake for 50–60 minutes until set but slightly jiggly in the center. Step 4: Cool completely, then refrigerate at least 4 hours or overnight. To serve, run a knife around the edge and invert onto a plate to release the caramel sauce.

menuItems.name: Arroz con Leche
menuItems.description: Creamy Mexican rice pudding, cinnamon, vanilla, raisins, coconut flakes
menuItems.method: Step 1: Rinse the rice under cold water until the water runs clear. In a medium saucepan, bring 2 cups of water to a boil and add the rinsed rice. Cook uncovered over medium heat for about 5 minutes, or until the water is mostly absorbed. Step 2: Add the whole milk, cinnamon stick, and sugar (if using). Simmer gently over low heat, stirring occasionally, for 20–25 minutes until the rice is tender and the mixture thickens. Step 3: Stir in the sweetened condensed milk, vanilla extract, raisins, and shredded coconut. Continue cooking for another 5–10 minutes until creamy and well combined. Remove the cinnamon stick before serving. Serve warm or chilled, garnished with extra cinnamon or coconut if desired.

menuItems.name: BuÃ±uelos con Piloncillo
menuItems.description: Thin crispy fried pastry, piloncillo syrup, cinnamon, anise, toasted pecans

menuItems.name: Greek Salad
menuItems.description: Tomatoes, cucumber, kalamata olives, feta cheese, red onion, oregano, olive oil
menuItems.method: Step 1: In a large bowl, combine the chopped tomatoes, sliced cucumber, kalamata olives, and thinly sliced red onion. Step 2: Add the feta cheese cubes or crumbles on top without overmixing to keep the cheese intact. Step 3: Sprinkle the dried oregano evenly over the salad. Step 4: Drizzle the extra virgin olive oil over the entire mixture. Gently toss just enough to coat the ingredients lightly while preserving the feta’s texture. Serve immediately at room temperature for the freshest flavor. For best results, use ripe but firm tomatoes and high-quality Greek feta. This traditional Greek salad requires no lettuce and relies on the natural juiciness of the vegetables and richness of the olive oil and cheese for its distinctive taste.

menuItems.name: Hummus Mezze Platter
menuItems.description: House hummus, baba ganoush, tabbouleh, pita bread, olives, falafel
menuItems.method: Step 1: Prepare hummus by blending chickpeas, tahini, lemon juice, garlic, cumin, salt, and 2 tbsp olive oil until smooth. Step 2: Roast eggplant at 400°F (200°C) for 40 minutes, then scoop flesh and mix with lemon juice, garlic, tahini, and olive oil for baba ganoush. Step 3: Soak bulgur in hot water for 15 minutes; drain and combine with parsley, tomatoes, cucumber, lemon juice, olive oil, and salt for tabbouleh. Step 4: Warm pita bread briefly in oven or on stovetop. Step 5: Arrange hummus, baba ganoush, tabbouleh, warm pita, olives, and falafel attractively on a large platter. Drizzle dips with olive oil and serve immediately.

menuItems.name: Grilled Octopus
menuItems.description: Charred octopus, lemon, capers, olive oil, cherry tomatoes, fresh herbs
menuItems.method: Step 1: Simmer the cleaned octopus in a large pot of salted water with a bay leaf for 45–60 minutes until tender; drain and cool slightly. Step 2: Preheat a grill or grill pan to high heat. Pat the octopus dry and brush with 1 tablespoon olive oil. Grill for 3–4 minutes per side until charred and crispy. Step 3: In a bowl, combine cherry tomatoes, capers, lemon juice and zest, remaining olive oil, parsley, oregano, salt, and pepper. Step 4: Slice the grilled octopus into bite-sized pieces and arrange on a platter. Spoon the tomato-caper mixture over the top. Drizzle with extra olive oil if desired and serve immediately.

menuItems.name: Lamb Souvlaki
menuItems.description: Grilled lamb skewers, tzatziki, pita, grilled vegetables, lemon
menuItems.method: Step 1: Cut lamb into 2.5cm cubes and marinate with olive oil, lemon juice, garlic, oregano, salt, and pepper for at least 2 hours or overnight. Step 2: Thread lamb onto soaked wooden or metal skewers. Grill over medium-high heat for 8–10 minutes, turning occasionally, until browned and cooked through. Step 3: While grilling, toss bell peppers and zucchini with olive oil, salt, and pepper; grill alongside the lamb until tender. Step 4: Mix grated cucumber (squeezed dry), Greek yogurt, red onion, a pinch of salt, and a drizzle of olive oil to make tzatziki. Step 5: Warm pita bread briefly on the grill. Serve souvlaki with grilled vegetables, tzatziki, warm pita, and lemon wedges.

menuItems.name: Spanakopita
menuItems.description: Spinach and feta phyllo pie, golden and flaky, served with Greek salad
menuItems.method: Step 1: Preheat oven to 350°F (175°C). Sauté onion and garlic in olive oil until soft. Add spinach and cook until wilted; drain excess liquid. Step 2: In a bowl, combine spinach mixture, crumbled feta, eggs, dill, salt, and pepper. Mix well. Step 3: Brush a baking dish with olive oil. Layer 8 phyllo sheets, brushing each with oil. Spread filling evenly over the phyllo. Step 4: Top with remaining 8 phyllo sheets, again brushing each with oil. Score the top into portions. Step 5: Bake for 45–50 minutes until golden and crisp. Let cool slightly before serving with Greek salad.

menuItems.name: Lemon Herb Branzino
menuItems.description: Whole Mediterranean sea bass, fresh herbs, lemon, capers, olive oil

ingredients.name: fresh herbs (such as thyme, parsley, and dill)
ingredients.amount: 1/4 cup chopped, plus extra sprigs for cavity

menuItems.method: Step 1: Preheat oven to 400°F (200°C). Pat the branzino dry and season inside and out with salt and pepper. Stuff the cavity with lemon slices and herb sprigs. Step 2: Place the fish on a parchment-lined baking sheet. Drizzle with 2 tablespoons olive oil and scatter chopped herbs and capers over the top. Roast for 20–25 minutes, or until the flesh flakes easily with a fork and reaches an internal temperature of 145°F. Step 3: Remove from oven, drizzle with remaining olive oil, and garnish with additional fresh herbs and lemon slices. Serve immediately with roasted vegetables or a simple salad.

menuItems.name: Falafel Wrap
menuItems.description: Crispy falafel, hummus, tomato, cucumber, pickled turnip, tahini, pita
menuItems.method: Step 1: Warm the pita breads in a dry skillet or oven until pliable but not crisp. Step 2: Lay each pita flat and spread 1½ tablespoons of hummus evenly over the center. Step 3: Place 3 crispy falafel balls down the middle of each pita. Step 4: Layer sliced tomato, cucumber, and chopped pickled turnip over the falafel. Step 5: Drizzle tahini sauce generously over the vegetables. Step 6: Fold the sides of the pita inward, then roll tightly from the bottom to enclose the filling. Step 7: Serve immediately, optionally wrapped in parchment paper for easy handling. For best results, use freshly fried falafel and room-temperature vegetables to maintain texture contrast.

menuItems.name: Baklava
menuItems.description: Layers of phyllo, walnuts, honey syrup, cinnamon, rosewater
menuItems.method: Step 1: Preheat oven to 350°F (175°C). Lightly grease a 9x13-inch baking dish. Step 2: In a bowl, mix chopped walnuts with cinnamon. Step 3: Layer 8 sheets of phyllo in the dish, brushing each with melted butter. Step 4: Sprinkle a third of the walnut mixture evenly over the phyllo. Repeat layers twice more, finishing with 8 buttered phyllo sheets on top. Step 5: Using a sharp knife, cut the unbaked baklava into diamond or square shapes. Step 6: Bake for 45–50 minutes until golden brown. Step 7: While baking, prepare syrup by boiling sugar, water, honey, and rosewater for 10 minutes; cool slightly. Step 8: Immediately after removing baklava from oven, pour cooled syrup evenly over it. Let sit at least 4 hours before serving to absorb syrup.

menuItems.name: Tzatziki & Warm Pita
menuItems.description: Thick strained yogurt, cucumber, garlic, dill, olive oil, warm house-baked pita
menuItems.method: Step 1: Place the grated cucumber in a clean kitchen towel and squeeze out as much liquid as possible. Step 2: In a bowl, combine the strained Greek yogurt, drained cucumber, minced garlic, chopped dill, olive oil, lemon juice, and salt. Mix well until smooth and evenly blended. Taste and adjust seasoning if needed. Step 3: Cover and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes to allow flavors to meld. Step 4: While the tzatziki chills, warm the pita bread in a dry skillet over medium heat for about 1–2 minutes per side, or until soft and slightly puffed. Alternatively, wrap in foil and warm in a 350°F (175°C) oven for 5–7 minutes. Step 5: Serve the chilled tzatziki alongside the warm pita for dipping.

menuItems.name: Dolmades
menuItems.description: Grape leaves stuffed with herb rice, lemon olive oil dressing, served warm
menuItems.method: Step 1: In a saucepan, sauté onion in 2 tablespoons olive oil until soft. Add rice and stir for 1 minute. Add broth, salt, and pepper; simmer covered for 10 minutes until rice is par-cooked. Remove from heat, fluff with a fork, and mix in dill, mint, parsley, and lemon juice. Cool slightly. Step 2: Lay a grape leaf vein-side up. Place 1 tablespoon filling near the stem end, fold sides inward, and roll tightly. Arrange rolls seam-down in a pot. Drizzle with remaining olive oil and add water to cover. Place a heat-safe plate on top to keep dolmades submerged. Simmer gently for 30–40 minutes until tender. Serve warm.

menuItems.name: Saganaki
menuItems.description: Pan-fried Kefalograviera cheese, flamed tableside, fresh lemon juice, crusty bread
menuItems.method: Step 1: Cut the Kefalograviera cheese into a thick slice (about 1 cm) and lightly dredge both sides in flour, shaking off excess. Step 2: Heat olive oil in a non-stick skillet over medium-high heat until shimmering. Carefully place the cheese in the pan and cook for 2–3 minutes per side until golden brown and slightly softened but still holding its shape. Step 3: Transfer the sizzling cheese to a heatproof plate or traditional saganaki pan. At the table, pour a splash of ouzo or brandy over the cheese (optional but traditional), then carefully ignite it with a long match for a dramatic flame—let it burn briefly before extinguishing. Step 4: Immediately squeeze fresh lemon juice over the melted cheese and serve hot with crusty bread for dipping.

menuItems.name: White Bean Skordalia
menuItems.description: Creamy white bean and garlic dip, olive oil, roasted garlic, served with cruditÃ©s
menuItems.method: Step 1: Drain and rinse the cooked cannellini beans if using canned. Step 2: In a food processor, combine the beans, roasted garlic cloves, lemon juice, salt, and pepper. Pulse until mostly smooth. Step 3: With the processor running, slowly drizzle in the olive oil until fully incorporated and creamy. Step 4: If the mixture is too thick, add water one tablespoon at a time until your desired dip consistency is reached. Step 5: Taste and adjust seasoning, adding more salt, pepper, or lemon juice as needed. Step 6: Transfer to a serving bowl, drizzle with a little extra olive oil, and serve chilled or at room temperature alongside an assortment of fresh crudités such as carrot sticks, cucumber rounds, bell pepper strips, and radishes.

menuItems.name: Greek Yogurt with Honey & Walnuts
menuItems.description: Thick Cretan yogurt, wild thyme honey, toasted walnuts, cinnamon
menuItems.method: Step 1: Toast the walnuts in a dry skillet over medium heat for 3–5 minutes, stirring frequently until fragrant and lightly browned. Let them cool slightly. Step 2: Scoop the Greek yogurt into a serving bowl or individual dishes. Drizzle generously with wild thyme honey, ensuring it pools slightly on top. Step 3: Sprinkle the toasted walnuts evenly over the yogurt. Finish with a light dusting of ground cinnamon for warmth and aroma. Serve immediately to enjoy the contrast of cool, creamy yogurt with the crunch of nuts and the floral sweetness of the honey. This traditional Greek dessert or breakfast requires no cooking beyond toasting the nuts and highlights high-quality ingredients for maximum flavor.

menuItems.name: Loukoumades
menuItems.description: Mini honey-dipped Greek doughnuts, cinnamon, crushed walnuts, sesame seeds
menuItems.method: Step 1: In a bowl, dissolve yeast and sugar in warm water; let sit for 5–10 minutes until frothy. Mix in flour and salt to form a soft dough. Cover and let rise in a warm place for 1 hour or until doubled. Step 2: Heat oil in a deep pan to 350°F (175°C). Drop tablespoon-sized dough balls into the oil and fry until golden brown, turning occasionally (about 2–3 minutes). Drain on paper towels. Step 3: Warm honey with cinnamon in a saucepan until slightly runny. Dip each fried dough ball into the honey mixture, then place on a serving plate. Sprinkle generously with crushed walnuts and sesame seeds. Serve warm.

menuItems.name: Galaktoboureko
menuItems.description: Crispy phyllo filled with semolina custard, soaked in lemon-scented syrup
menuItems.method: Step 1: Preheat oven to 350°F (175°C). Butter a 9x13-inch baking dish. Layer half the phyllo sheets in the dish, brushing each with melted butter. Step 2: In a saucepan, heat milk and semolina over medium heat, stirring constantly until thickened (about 10 minutes). Remove from heat, stir in sugar, vanilla, and let cool slightly. Beat eggs and gradually whisk into the semolina mixture. Pour this custard over the phyllo layers. Step 3: Top with remaining phyllo sheets, again buttering each layer. Score the top into diamonds or squares. Bake for 45–50 minutes until golden brown. Step 4: While baking, prepare syrup by boiling water, sugar, lemon juice, and zest for 10 minutes. Immediately after removing the pastry from the oven, pour the hot syrup evenly over it. Let cool completely before serving.

menuItems.name: Revani
menuItems.description: Moist Greek semolina cake soaked in orange syrup, shredded coconut, fresh orange zest
menuItems.method: Step 1: Preheat oven to 350°F (175°C). Grease and flour a 9x13-inch baking pan. Step 2: In a bowl, whisk together semolina, flour, and baking powder. In another bowl, beat eggs and sugar until pale and fluffy. Gradually add oil, orange juice, and zest, mixing well. Fold in dry ingredients and shredded coconut until just combined. Pour batter into the pan and bake for 30–35 minutes or until golden and a toothpick comes out clean. Step 3: While cake bakes, prepare syrup by simmering water, sugar, and orange juice for 10 minutes until slightly thickened. Step 4: Immediately after removing cake from oven, pierce surface with a fork and pour warm syrup evenly over it. Let cool completely before serving.

menuItems.name: Chicken Tikka Masala
menuItems.description: Tender chicken in creamy tomato-based tikka masala sauce, basmati rice, naan
menuItems.method: Step 1: Marinate chicken in yogurt, lemon juice, garlic, ginger, 1 tsp garam masala, cumin, and turmeric for at least 1 hour. Grill or pan-sear until cooked through. Step 2: In a pan, heat oil and sauté onion until golden. Add remaining garam masala and tomato puree; simmer 10 minutes. Stir in cream and cooked chicken; cook 5 more minutes. Step 3: Meanwhile, rinse basmati rice and cook according to package instructions until fluffy. Step 4: Warm naan in a dry skillet or oven. Serve chicken tikka masala over rice with warm naan on the side.

menuItems.name: Dal Tadka
menuItems.description: Yellow lentils tempered with cumin, mustard seeds, garlic, tomatoes, served with rice
menuItems.method: Step 1: Rinse the yellow lentils thoroughly and cook them in 3 cups of water with turmeric and salt until soft and mushy, about 20–25 minutes. Mash lightly and set aside. Step 2: In a separate pan, heat ghee or oil. Add mustard seeds and let them splutter. Add cumin seeds, then sauté chopped onions until golden. Add minced garlic and green chilies; cook for 1 minute. Stir in chopped tomatoes, red chili powder, and cook until tomatoes break down and oil separates. Step 3: Pour this tempering into the cooked dal, mix well, and simmer for 5 minutes. Adjust salt and consistency with water if needed. Garnish with fresh cilantro and serve hot with steamed rice.

menuItems.name: Palak Paneer
menuItems.description: Creamy spinach curry with fresh paneer, garam masala, ginger, garlic, naan
menuItems.method: Step 1: Blanch spinach in boiling water for 2–3 minutes, then blend into a smooth puree. Step 2: Heat oil or ghee in a pan, add cumin seeds and let them sizzle. Add chopped onions and sauté until golden. Stir in ginger, garlic, and green chili; cook for 1–2 minutes. Add tomatoes and cook until soft and oil separates. Step 3: Mix in turmeric, garam masala, and salt. Cook for another minute. Step 4: Add spinach puree and simmer for 5–7 minutes. Stir in cream or yogurt. Step 5: Cut paneer into cubes, lightly fry if desired, then add to the curry. Simmer for 3–4 minutes to blend flavors. Serve hot with naan.

menuItems.name: Lamb Biryani
menuItems.description: Fragrant basmati rice, slow-cooked lamb, saffron, whole spices, raita, mint
