ingredients.name: whole spices (cinnamon stick, cardamom pods, cloves)

menuItems.method: Step 1: Soak basmati rice in water for 30 minutes, then parboil with whole spices until 70% cooked; drain and set aside. Step 2: Marinate lamb with yogurt, ginger-garlic paste, salt, and half the mint for 1 hour. Step 3: Heat oil or ghee in a heavy pot; sauté onions until golden. Add marinated lamb and cook on medium heat until browned and tender (about 30–40 minutes). Step 4: Warm saffron in 2 tablespoons of milk or water. Layer half the rice over the lamb, sprinkle with saffron liquid and remaining mint, then top with remaining rice. Step 5: Cover tightly and cook on low heat (dum style) for 20–25 minutes. Let rest 10 minutes before gently fluffing layers together. Serve with raita.

menuItems.name: Samosa Chaat
menuItems.description: Crispy samosas, chickpea curry, yogurt, tamarind chutney, mint chutney
menuItems.method: Step 1: Arrange the chopped samosas on a serving plate. Step 2: Top with cooked chickpeas, chopped onion, and tomato. Step 3: Drizzle yogurt evenly over the mixture. Step 4: Add generous swirls of tamarind chutney and mint-cilantro chutney. Step 5: Sprinkle chaat masala, roasted cumin powder, and fresh cilantro over the top. Step 6: Finish with a handful of sev for crunch. Serve immediately to maintain texture contrast between crispy samosas and soft toppings. For best results, use freshly fried samosas and chilled yogurt. Adjust chutney quantities to taste—more tamarind for tanginess or more mint for freshness. This popular Indian street food balances sweet, sour, spicy, and savory flavors in every bite.

menuItems.name: Aloo Gobi
menuItems.description: Dry-spiced cauliflower and potato, turmeric, cumin, coriander, green chili
menuItems.method: Step 1: Heat oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add cumin seeds and let them sizzle for 30 seconds until fragrant. Step 2: Add chopped onions and sauté until golden brown. If using tomato, add it now and cook until soft. Step 3: Stir in turmeric, coriander powder, and green chilies; cook for 1 minute to release aromas. Step 4: Add potatoes and cauliflower florets. Mix well to coat with spices. Step 5: Cover and cook on low-medium heat for 15–20 minutes, stirring occasionally, until vegetables are tender but not mushy. Add a splash of water if needed to prevent sticking. Step 6: Season with salt to taste. Garnish with fresh cilantro before serving hot with roti or rice.

menuItems.name: Tandoori Prawns
menuItems.description: Jumbo prawns marinated in yogurt and spices, grilled in tandoor, mint chutney
menuItems.method: Step 1: Clean and devein the prawns, leaving tails intact. In a bowl, mix yogurt, lemon juice, ginger-garlic paste, tandoori masala, turmeric, red chili powder, salt, and oil to make the marinade. Add prawns and coat well. Marinate for at least 2 hours, preferably overnight. Step 2: Skewer the prawns and grill in a preheated tandoor or oven at 220°C (425°F) for 8–10 minutes, turning once, until opaque and slightly charred. Meanwhile, blend mint leaves, green chilies, cilantro, and lime juice into a smooth mint chutney. Serve hot grilled prawns with the mint chutney on the side.

menuItems.name: Gulab Jamun
menuItems.description: Soft milk-solid dumplings soaked in rose-scented sugar syrup, served warm
menuItems.method: Step 1: Knead khoya, flour, and baking soda into a soft, smooth dough. Rest for 10 minutes. Step 2: Divide into small balls, ensuring no cracks. Heat ghee or oil on low flame and gently fry the balls until golden brown, turning often for even cooking. Step 3: While frying, prepare syrup by boiling sugar and water for 5–7 minutes until slightly sticky. Add rose water and cardamom powder. Step 4: Once dumplings are cooked, immediately transfer them into warm syrup. Let them soak for at least 1–2 hours to absorb flavor and soften further. Serve warm or at room temperature. Avoid over-kneading the dough to keep jamuns soft, and maintain low oil temperature to prevent browning too quickly while ensuring they cook through.

menuItems.name: Papdi Chaat
menuItems.description: Crispy semolina wafers, spiced chickpeas, yogurt, tamarind chutney, mint chutney, sev
menuItems.method: Step 1: Arrange the papdi wafers on a serving plate. Step 2: Spoon boiled chickpeas evenly over the wafers. Step 3: Drizzle yogurt gently over the top, followed by tamarind and mint-coriander chutneys in zigzag patterns. Step 4: Sprinkle roasted cumin powder, chaat masala, and red chili powder evenly. Step 5: Generously scatter sev over the entire dish and garnish with chopped fresh coriander leaves. Serve immediately to maintain crispness. Papdi Chaat is best enjoyed fresh so the wafers stay crunchy while absorbing just enough of the tangy, creamy sauces for a balanced burst of sweet, spicy, and savory flavors in every bite.

menuItems.name: Onion Bhaji
menuItems.description: Crispy spiced onion fritters, chickpea batter, coriander, cumin, green chili, mint chutney

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.amount: as needed to make a thick batter

menuItems.method: Step 1: In a large bowl, mix chickpea flour, ground cumin, baking powder, salt, chopped green chili, and fresh coriander. Gradually add water to form a thick, smooth batter. Step 2: Fold in the thinly sliced onions until evenly coated. Let the mixture rest for 10–15 minutes. Step 3: Heat oil in a deep pan over medium heat. Drop spoonfuls of the batter into the hot oil, flattening slightly with the back of the spoon. Fry 2–3 at a time until golden brown and crisp, about 2–3 minutes per side. Step 4: Drain on paper towels. Serve hot with mint chutney.

menuItems.name: Seekh Kebab
menuItems.description: Spiced minced lamb skewers grilled in tandoor, chaat masala, green chutney, onion rings
menuItems.method: Step 1: In a large bowl, combine minced lamb, chopped onion, ginger-garlic paste, green chilies, coriander leaves, chaat masala, garam masala, cumin powder, salt, and lemon juice. Mix thoroughly until the mixture becomes slightly sticky and holds together. Step 2: Cover and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes to allow flavors to meld. Step 3: Soak wooden skewers in water for 20 minutes if using. Shape the meat mixture around metal or soaked wooden skewers into cylindrical kebabs. Step 4: Grill in a preheated tandoor, oven broiler, or on a barbecue over medium-high heat for 10–12 minutes, turning occasionally, until cooked through and slightly charred. Serve hot with onion rings and green chutney.

menuItems.name: Tomato Shorba
menuItems.description: Spiced Indian tomato soup, ginger, cardamom, coriander, fresh cream, pappadom
menuItems.method: Step 1: Heat oil or ghee in a pot. Sauté chopped onion until golden, then add minced garlic and grated ginger; cook for 1 minute. Step 2: Add cardamom pods and chopped tomatoes. Cook until tomatoes break down and become pulpy (8–10 minutes). Step 3: Pour in water, season with salt, and simmer for 15 minutes. Remove cardamom pods. Step 4: Blend the mixture until smooth, then strain for a silky texture. Return to heat, stir in fresh cream, and warm gently without boiling. Step 5: Garnish with chopped coriander and serve hot with crisp pappadoms on the side.

menuItems.name: Mango Kulfi
menuItems.description: Traditional Indian frozen dessert with Alphonso mango, cardamom, saffron, pistachios
menuItems.method: Step 1: Soak saffron strands in 1 tablespoon of warm milk for 10 minutes to release color and flavor. Step 2: In a large bowl, whisk together Alphonso mango pulp, sweetened condensed milk, and heavy cream until smooth and well combined. Step 3: Stir in the soaked saffron (with milk) and cardamom powder. Mix thoroughly. Step 4: Pour the mixture into kulfi molds or small freezer-safe containers. Tap gently to remove air bubbles. Step 5: Sprinkle chopped pistachios on top and press lightly so they adhere. Step 6: Freeze for at least 6–8 hours or overnight until completely firm. Step 7: To unmold, briefly dip the molds in warm water for 10–15 seconds, then gently slide out the kulfi. Serve immediately.

menuItems.name: Rasmalai
menuItems.description: Soft cottage cheese dumplings in sweetened saffron milk, cardamom, rose water, pistachios

ingredients.name: lemon juice or vinegar
ingredients.amount: 2 tablespoons (for curdling milk, if making paneer from scratch)

menuItems.method: Step 1: If not using store-bought paneer, heat 1 liter of milk until boiling, add lemon juice or vinegar to curdle, strain through muslin, and press to form soft paneer. Knead until smooth. Step 2: Divide paneer into small balls, flatten slightly, and gently boil in water for 10–12 minutes until spongy. Drain and cool. Step 3: In a separate pan, simmer another liter of milk until reduced by half. Add sugar, saffron, and cardamom; stir until dissolved. Cool slightly, then add rose water. Step 4: Gently place the cooked paneer dumplings into the sweetened milk. Refrigerate for at least 2 hours. Garnish with chopped pistachios before serving.

menuItems.name: Gajar Halwa
menuItems.description: Slow-cooked carrot pudding, ghee, full cream milk, cardamom, cashews, raisins, warm
menuItems.method: Step 1: Heat ghee in a heavy-bottomed pan over medium heat. Add grated carrots and sauté for 5–7 minutes until softened. Step 2: Pour in the milk and cook on low heat, stirring occasionally, until the milk reduces completely and the mixture thickens (about 30–40 minutes). Step 3: Add sugar and cardamom powder, mixing well. Continue cooking for another 10–15 minutes until the halwa pulls away from the sides of the pan. Step 4: In a small pan, lightly fry cashews and raisins in a teaspoon of ghee until golden. Stir them into the halwa or use as garnish. Serve warm or at room temperature. The slow cooking ensures deep flavor and a rich, pudding-like consistency.

menuItems.name: Jalebi
menuItems.description: Crispy deep-fried fermented batter spirals soaked in saffron sugar syrup, served warm
menuItems.method: Step 1: Prepare the batter by mixing all-purpose flour, cornstarch, and yogurt. Gradually add water to form a smooth, thick batter. Cover and let it ferment for 8–12 hours or overnight until slightly bubbly. Step 2: For the syrup, combine sugar, water, saffron, and cardamom in a saucepan. Simmer until it reaches one-string consistency (about 5–7 minutes), then keep warm. Step 3: Heat oil in a deep pan over medium heat. Transfer fermented batter into a squeeze bottle or piping bag. Swirl thin spirals directly into the hot oil and fry until golden and crisp. Step 4: Immediately dip each fried jalebi into the warm saffron syrup for 10–15 seconds. Serve warm.

menuItems.name: French Onion Soup
menuItems.description: Slow-caramelized onion broth, GruyÃ¨re crouton, fresh thyme
menuItems.method: Step 1: In a large pot, melt butter with olive oil over medium heat. Add sliced onions and cook slowly, stirring occasionally, until deeply caramelized (about 45 minutes). Step 2: Add white wine to deglaze the pot, scraping up browned bits; simmer until reduced by half. Step 3: Pour in beef broth, add thyme sprigs and bay leaf, then season with salt and pepper. Simmer gently for 30 minutes. Step 4: Preheat broiler. Ladle soup into oven-safe bowls. Top each with a baguette slice and generous Gruyère. Broil until cheese is bubbly and golden. Serve hot.

menuItems.name: Duck Confit
menuItems.description: Slow-cooked duck leg, lentil du Puy, roasted root vegetables, red wine reduction
menuItems.method: Step 1: Season duck legs with salt, pepper, garlic, and thyme; refrigerate overnight. Step 2: Preheat oven to 300°F (150°C). Rinse seasoning off duck legs, pat dry, and place in a deep ovenproof dish. Cover completely with melted duck fat. Cook for 2.5–3 hours until tender. Step 3: Meanwhile, roast carrots and parsnips tossed in olive oil at 400°F (200°C) for 25 minutes. Simmer lentils in water until just tender, about 20–25 minutes. Step 4: For the reduction, simmer red wine until reduced by half, then add stock and reduce further to syrupy consistency. Step 5: Crisp duck skin in a hot pan, then serve atop lentils with roasted vegetables and drizzle with red wine reduction.

menuItems.name: Croque Monsieur
menuItems.description: Ham and GruyÃ¨re toasted sandwich, bÃ©chamel sauce, Dijon mustard
menuItems.method: Step 1: Preheat oven to 375°F (190°C). Butter one side of each bread slice. Spread Dijon mustard on the unbuttered side of one slice. Layer ham and half the Gruyère on top, then cap with the second bread slice, buttered side out. Step 2: Make béchamel by melting butter in a saucepan, whisking in flour to form a roux, then gradually adding milk while stirring until smooth and thickened. Season with salt, pepper, and nutmeg. Spread béchamel over the top of the sandwich, then sprinkle remaining Gruyère on top. Step 3: Place on a baking sheet and bake for 10–15 minutes until golden and bubbly. Alternatively, broil for 2–3 minutes for a quicker finish.

menuItems.description: Airy dark chocolate mousse, 70% Valrhona chocolate, sea salt, candied orange
menuItems.method: Step 1: Melt the dark chocolate gently over a double boiler or in short bursts in the microwave, stirring until smooth. Let cool slightly. Step 2: Separate the eggs. Whisk egg yolks with sugar until pale and slightly thickened, then fold into the melted chocolate along with sea salt. Step 3: In a separate bowl, whip the heavy cream to soft peaks and set aside. Step 4: In another clean bowl, beat egg whites to stiff peaks. Gently fold the whipped cream into the chocolate mixture, then carefully fold in the egg whites until no streaks remain. Step 5: Spoon the mousse into serving glasses or ramekins, cover, and chill for at least 4 hours or overnight. Before serving, sprinkle with finely chopped candied orange peel for a bright, citrusy finish.

menuItems.method: Step 1: Preheat oven to 425°F (220°C). In a saucepan, bring water and butter to a boil. Remove from heat, add flour all at once, and stir vigorously until smooth. Return to low heat for 1–2 minutes to dry the dough. Transfer to a bowl and let cool slightly. Step 2: Beat in eggs one at a time until glossy and thick. Pipe or spoon into 1-inch mounds on a parchment-lined baking sheet. Bake 15 minutes, then reduce heat to 375°F (190°C) and bake 15–20 more minutes until golden and hollow. Cool completely. Step 3: Whip heavy cream with powdered sugar and vanilla until stiff peaks form. Slice cooled puffs and fill with Chantilly cream. Step 4: Melt dark chocolate gently and drizzle over filled profiteroles. Garnish with toasted almonds.
